question: How much of round 1's failure was the model and how much the way the engine calls it? Same figures, truth, scorer and judge prompt; a reworked engine around three of the round-1 models.
figures: the 15 of ../testset.json (10 data charts, 560 truth values in 33 panels; 5 without data)
bundles: samples/aca-papers_out, converted with extrct_docling-v2.131.0-r4, default configuration (unchanged from round 1)

engine.state: docling/engines/figure_data as changed in this round (LOG.md section 3), on top of the round-1 commit; frozen before the three runs below
engine.ocr: RapidOCR (onnxruntime, PP-OCRv6 small detection and recognition) on the work image, about 1 to 4 s per figure on CPU

reference_run.name: claude-sonnet-5-5-blind
reference_run.what: one claude-sonnet-5-5 sub-agent given the 15 work images only; not a model inside the engine and not a candidate (cloud)

ablation.no_split: the round-2 engine with --panel-split gutters (the round-1 splitter; the overview gate still runs, the agreement rule does not)

hardware.gpu: NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark, unified memory), one model loaded at a time, nothing else on the GPU
hardware.ollama: 0.32.14 (image budget for Gemma 4 capped at about 270 tokens; see LOG.md F9)

judge.judge_agent: one general-purpose sub-agent per run, fresh context, tools on, read-only on the repository
judge.prompt: judge/PROMPT.md (the round-1 prompt with round-2 paths and a rule for figures the engine declines)
judge.isolation: a judge reads one run's outputs only, no other judge's file and nothing of round 1
